listing_note: Euronext Amsterdam ordinary listing (AEX constituent), reports in EUR. Same company as the US OTC ADR ADYEY (1 ADS = 1/100th of one ADYEN.AS ordinary share); this is the EUR primary-listing file, refreshed after the Q3 2026 Business Update (28 Oct 2026: unaudited, revenue-only, no P&L or balance sheet) and market reaction through 30 Oct 2026. Profit, SBC and cash data therefore still come from the 13 Aug 2026 H1 letter. The top line is net revenue; quarterly updates overlap the H1/H2 periods and must not be summed with them.
overview: Adyen is a Dutch fintech running one self-built global platform that combines payment acquiring, processing, risk/fraud management and (via its own EU, US and UK banking licenses) embedded financial products such as issuing, accounts and capital. It serves large enterprises and software platforms/marketplaces (Uber, Spotify, Meta, McDonald's, eBay, Etsy, Starbucks, LVMH, Toast, Lufthansa) across Digital, Unified Commerce (online plus in-store) and Platforms, and since July 2026 also owns Talon.One (loyalty/promotions) and Orb (usage-based billing). Q3 2026 net revenue was €738.1mn (+23%, +22% constant currency, ~20% organic) on €451.1bn of volume (+30%), but on 28 Oct Adyen cut its 2026 EBITDA margin guide to 50% and discontinued its 'above 55% by 2028' objective to fund an accelerated hiring and investment cycle. EMEA is ~55% of H1 2026 net revenue, North America ~27%, APAC ~11%, LATAM ~7%.

business_model.description: Adyen earns a small percentage ('take rate') plus fixed fees on payment volume processed for merchants, net of interchange and scheme fees. Owning the full stack (gateway, processing, acquiring, risk) and its banking licenses gives one global integration and room to monetize adjacent products: issuing, capital, accounts, money movement and, since July 2026, loyalty (Talon.One) and billing (Orb). Payments remain the vast majority of revenue and are volume-driven, but relationships are sticky and compound via land-and-expand: share of wallet rises from under 20% in years 3-7 to over 40% after year 12, ~two-thirds of H1 2026 growth came from customers onboarded in 2024 or earlier, and the top 300 merchants drive ~60% of growth (>70% three years ago). Talon.One and Orb add recurring revenue with no processed volume (~2 points of Q3 growth). Tiered pricing passes scale benefits to large customers, so revenue grows slower than volume (Q3: +22% CC vs +30%). No dividend and no buyback; capital priorities per the Q3 call are regulatory/operational capital, organic growth, bolt-on M&A, then shareholder returns. Compensation 'increasingly emphasizes equity-based incentives', so with no buyback offset SBC is a rising cost and a dilution source.

revenue_streams.name: Digital
revenue_streams.description: Payments for online-first enterprises: subscription/media, travel, mobility, digital marketplaces, financial services
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~52% of Q3 2026 net revenue: €387.4mn, +16% YoY / +14% CC (H1: +13% / +15% CC; Q1: +9% / +13% CC); volume +28%, implying ~9% lower yield per euro (derived). Slowest pillar; Q3 driven by wallet-share gains with the largest customers (travel & mobility, content & subscriptions)

revenue_streams.name: Unified Commerce
revenue_streams.description: Combined online and in-store payments for global retail, hospitality, food & beverage, entertainment and travel merchants; home of Talon.One
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~34% of Q3: €250.5mn, +29% / +27% CC (H1: +25% / +27% CC); volume +22%. Revenue outran volume because Talon.One adds recurring revenue with no volume, so organic growth is likely low-to-mid 20s (derived). 499 customers at scale across channels (486 at H1); 'subdued retail environment'

revenue_streams.name: Platforms
revenue_streams.description: Embedded payments and financial products (issuing, capital, accounts, now usage-based billing via Orb) for SaaS platforms and marketplaces (e.g., eBay, Etsy, Lightspeed, Fresha)
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~14% of Q3: €100.2mn, +46% / +44% CC (H1: +37% / +40% CC); volume +55%. 46 customers processing >€1bn annually (37 last quarter, 31 a year ago); 312k active business customers (+48%); share gains in financial services and insurance. Fastest-growing pillar and the home for Orb

revenue_streams.name: Net interest income
revenue_streams.description: Interest on merchant balances in Accounts/Capital products (inside net revenue) plus finance income on own cash (below EBITDA)
revenue_streams.approx_share: Net interest income €8.6mn in H1 2026 (not disclosed for Q3). Separately €143.2mn of finance income on own cash (H1 2025: €138.7mn) sits below EBITDA and is eroding with rates

business_model.customer_type: Large enterprise (B2B) merchants and software platforms/marketplaces, skewed to big multi-region customers; Platforms reaches smaller merchants through software partners. Customers include Uber, Spotify, Meta, McDonald's, eBay, Etsy, Starbucks, LVMH, Lufthansa, Toast (US expansion in H1 2026), Tod's, GOV.UK Pay, On Running, Navan, iFood. Per the Q3 call ~10% of volume now comes from a few hyperscale/cloud/AI-native companies; Orb is an entry point to AI-native software (payments wins: Route, Wasabi Technologies). Agentic-commerce partners include OpenAI, American Express, Mastercard, Salesforce, Visa.
business_model.geographic_mix: H1 2026 net revenue (no regional split in Q3): EMEA €722.5mn (55%, +15% CC), North America €358.1mn (27%, +30% CC), APAC €136.9mn (11%, +26% CC), LATAM €85.3mn (7%, +35% CC). Take rate (net revenue / volume): 16.2bps in H1 2026 (16.8bps H1 2025); Q3 2026 16.4bps (738.1/451.1) vs 17.2bps in Q3 2025, 16.3bps in Q1 and 16.2bps in Q2 2026. The uptick vs Q2 is NOT a recovery: Talon.One/Orb add ~€12mn of revenue (~2 points of growth) with no volume, so the organic take rate was ~16.1bps (derived), flat sequentially.
business_model.balance_sheet_caveat: Reported cash (€12.4bn at 30 Jun 2026) is overwhelmingly merchant settlement float, not shareholder capital. Own cash was €4.9bn, or ~€4.6bn after the Talon.One (€750mn, €69.8mn in shares) and Orb ($335mn, $33.2mn in shares) consideration; both deals closed 1 July. No financial debt, only IFRS-16 leases (€409mn). The Q3 update has no balance sheet; management said on the call that S&P raised its outlook to positive (A- affirmed).

competitive_position.market_position: Tier-1 enterprise payments player alongside Stripe in large-enterprise/complex commerce; share of the vast, fragmented global TAM remains modest. Dominant with large multi-channel merchants (retail, luxury, travel, marketplaces) that want one global platform; still building North America and the SMB/platform tail where Stripe is structurally stronger; Braintree (PayPal) is adding enterprise in-store processing against Unified Commerce. Q3 volume +30% ('continued to outperform our market') and Platforms share gains in financial services and insurance show no visible share loss, but yield is eroding (group take rate 16.4bps vs 17.2bps; Digital volume +28% vs revenue +14% CC), and the June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision plus the October margin reset keep the pricing-power and cost-of-growth debates open.

moat_factors.description: One codebase across gateway, processing, acquiring and risk avoids the multi-vendor stacks of legacy processors (Fiserv, FIS, Worldpay) and Stripe's more modular approach; consistent performance and unified data across channels. Hiring is focused on specialized technical and go-to-market roles, particularly in the US

EU credit institution, US Federal Foreign Branch and UK PRA/FCA licenses let Adyen run acquiring, issuing, accounts and capital natively; H1 2026 added a UAE Category II payments license and direct STET (France) clearing membership. A regulatory barrier few rivals replicate

moat_factors.factor: Unified Commerce (online + in-store on one platform)
moat_factors.description: 499 customers process at scale across channels (459 a year ago) and the platform has 878k transacting terminals (+25%); Talon.One bridges online/offline loyalty, a gap standalone systems cannot. Braintree's in-store push is the first credible challenge, and retail is described as 'subdued'

Disclosed share-of-wallet curve (under 20% in years 3-7, over 40% after year 12); Q3 growth again came from wallet share with existing customers plus 'a healthy cohort of new enterprise merchants'. Flip side: tiered pricing hands scale benefits to the largest customers

Real-time risk and conversion layer (Adyen Uplift) delivered +0.9pp average conversion uplift by end-H1 2026 (On Running +0.85% conversion, -0.17% fraud rate); Authenticate was upgraded in Q3 with 'double-digit conversion gains' (company claim). Talon.One and Orb are built on the same layer

Talon.One (300+ brands) and Orb add adjacent, high-switching-cost infrastructure. Q3 evidence is encouraging but anecdotal: interest 'substantially stronger and broader than anticipated' and Orb customers Route and Wasabi moved payments volume to Adyen. Closed 1 July 2026, so too early to call proven

weaknesses: Take rate 16.4bps in Q3 2026 (organic ~16.1bps) vs 17.2bps a year earlier and 16.8bps in H1 2025: management cites 'expected volume tiering', but it looks similar to competitive discounting, and Adyen itself revised large-merchant pricing in June 2026
Digital, still the largest pillar (~52% of Q3), grew only +14% CC (H1 +15%, Q1 +13%) despite volume +28%
Concentration: top 300 merchants drive ~60% of growth (improving from >70%) and ~10% of volume sits with a few hyperscale/cloud companies
Sub-scale in North America versus incumbents and Stripe's home market, though North America was the fastest-growing region in H1 2026 (+30% CC)

Guidance credibility: Feb 2026 growth guide cut, May CFO exit, June pricing revision, and on 28 Oct a margin cut plus withdrawal of the 55%+ by 2028 target, 11 weeks after the H1 letter reaffirmed it and five weeks after a CFO release that, per its text, left financial objectives unchanged (AlphaValue headline: 'Broken promises come at a price')
No medium-term margin target to hold management to; the 'around 20%' growth view from Nov 2025 was called 'more kind of a guardrail as opposed to guidance' on the Q3 call
CapEx at 7% of net revenue in 2026 (from 'up to 5%') on a pull-forward of 2027 data-center spend amid supply-chain constraints

business.risk: Competitive intensity from Stripe, Braintree/PayPal, Checkout.com
business.description: Stripe is moving upmarket (Microsoft, Nvidia), Braintree is adding enterprise in-store processing and Checkout.com competes in European online; Adyen's own June 2026 pricing revision is evidence of price competition. Q3 shows no visible share loss, but yield per euro is falling

business.risk: Open-ended investment cycle / no margin anchor
business.description: 2026 margin cut to 50% (prior guide ~51.7%; FY2025 52.7%) and the 55%+ by 2028 objective discontinued 'to retain flexibility'. Management would not call 50% a floor, is 'intentionally' pulling spend forward, has no 2027 margin number until February (CFO: net revenue guide plus 'some color' on EBITDA/CapEx) and will not promise faster growth. FY 50% implies an H2 margin of ~50-51% vs 55.0% in H2 2025, i.e. H2 cash opex up ~35% on ~23% revenue growth (derived). Precedent: margin fell from 58.6% (H1 2022) to 43.3% (H1 2023) and only regained 55% in H2 2025

Group take rate 16.4bps in Q3 2026 vs 17.2bps in Q3 2025 (-5%), 16.3bps in Q1 and 16.2bps in Q2. The Q2-to-Q3 uptick is acquired non-volume revenue; the organic rate was ~16.1bps (derived). Q3 2025 revenue was lifted partly by settlement timing, so the YoY gap overstates the decline; the cleaner read is a flat ~16.1-16.4bps range for three quarters, stabilizing rather than recovering. Digital volume +28% vs revenue +14% CC implies ~9% lower yield

Q3 volume +30% (H1 +24%, Q1 +21%) laps a weak Q3 2025 base (+8% reported; +19% excluding a single large-volume customer), so part of the acceleration is mechanical. Revenue is growing 7-8 points slower than volume, and ~10% of volume comes from a few hyperscale/cloud companies

Digital +14% CC in Q3 vs Unified Commerce +27% (incl. Talon.One) and Platforms +44%; growth leans on wallet-share gains with the largest customers at lower yield. If those customers have permanently moved to a lower blended tier, group margin expansion is capped even if revenue holds

Talon.One and Orb (399 FTEs) are consolidated from Q3 and management is 'intentionally accelerating' investment behind both; the CFO said they 'are not standalone', so costs are ongoing. Contribution (~2 points of growth, similar in Q4) will be given only qualitatively on a combined basis, limiting return tracking. Co-CEO Uytdehaage leads integration

CFO Tandowsky left 31 Aug; Hwa Tsao is interim CFO until 1 Feb 2027, when Niclas Neglen (ex-Klarna CFO) is due to start, subject to an EGM vote and DNB approval. Supervisory Board chair Overmars retires 1 Nov (Herna Verhagen succeeds; Chris Vogelzang joined 7 Oct) and an undisclosed 'executive leadership model' update takes effect 31 Jan 2027. New CPO (1 Jul) and APAC president (1 Aug). Co-founder/co-CEO van der Does has reduced his day-to-day role for health reasons and was not among the Q3 call hosts

financial.description: 'Our compensation structure increasingly emphasizes equity-based incentives.' SBC sits inside EBITDA (wages and salaries), so it feeds the margin cut, and with no buybacks it dilutes holders. SBC was 1.84% of FY2025 net revenue (€43.5mn) and ~2.2% in H1 2026 (€29.1mn vs €19.6mn); the CFO called equity pay 'a material contributor to the change as we go forward' and gave no 2027 number. Shares drifted from 30.5mn (2020) to 31.567mn (Jun 2026), but the trend is now upward

financial.risk: CapEx step-up to 7% of net revenue
financial.description: Maintained at Q3, with a return 'towards historical levels post-2026'. H1 CapEx was €64.1mn (5%), so the target implies ~€135-140mn or ~9% of H2 net revenue (derived), alongside the margin cut. H1 FCF conversion was 86% of EBITDA

financial.risk: Net income sensitivity to interest rates
financial.description: Finance income on own cash was €143.2mn in H1 2026 vs €138.7mn despite a larger balance; further rate cuts compress below-EBITDA income (H1 net income +13% vs EBITDA +18%)
Q3 net revenue +23% reported vs +22% CC (a ~1pt tailwind) after a ~4pt headwind in Q1 and ~2pt in H1; USD revenue and the USD-priced Orb deal create translation risk
Purchase price allocation for Talon.One and Orb was unfinished at H1; goodwill and intangibles create a new impairment risk, and faster spending raises the return hurdle

regulatory.description: Credit-institution license (DNB) plus US, UK and UAE licenses bring capital, AML/KYC and prudential obligations; PwC reaches its maximum term after the FY2026 audit, so a new auditor is needed for FY2027

Interchange caps, open banking and payment-method mandates shape merchant economics. Adyen joined the ECB digital euro pilot as an acquiring PSP (36 PSPs selected 14 Jul 2026; 12-month pilot from H2 2027; legislation-dependent, readiness aimed for 2029): an option on a new rail with uncertain economics

Dynamic Identification, Adyen Uplift/Authenticate and Adyen Agentic raise exposure to the EU AI Act and GDPR; agentic-commerce standards (including the Sierra/Meta Personal Agent Protocol Adyen supports) are early and competing

macro.description: Volume tracks consumer spend. Q3 volume +30% shows no macro constraint, but Unified Commerce is growing 'amid a subdued retail environment' (company wording)
Tariff shifts push some customers into new regions (a tailwind for a multi-market platform) but add volume volatility
Rate cuts lower net income growth relative to EBITDA growth, as already visible in H1 2026

growth_drivers: Land-and-expand with existing enterprise customers: wallet-share gains with the largest Digital customers (travel & mobility, content & subscriptions) and a disclosed share-of-wallet curve from under 20% to over 40%

Platforms: +44% CC in Q3 and ~14% of net revenue; 46 customers >€1bn (31 a year ago), 312k active business customers (+48%), share gains in financial services and insurance, embedded capital/accounts/issuing

Orb as the AI-native billing wedge: usage-based billing is becoming the default for AI/software companies; payments wins from Orb's base (Route, Wasabi Technologies); management says joint demand is 'substantially stronger and broader than anticipated'
Talon.One cross-sell: in-store plus online loyalty for 300+ brands (many already Adyen customers), ~2 points of Q3 growth and a similar Q4 contribution expected
Unified Commerce: 499 customers at scale, 878k transacting terminals (+25%) and omnichannel loyalty via Talon.One
Intelligent Money Movement (Etsy, Expedia, Vinted) and embedded financial products (capital, accounts, issuing)

Agentic commerce and authentication: Adyen Agentic (partners incl. OpenAI, American Express, Mastercard, Salesforce, Visa), Personal Agent Protocol work with Sierra and Meta, upgraded Authenticate; ECB digital euro pilot as an option on a new rail

North America and US talent: fastest-growing region in H1 2026 (+30% CC); Q3 hiring focused on technical and go-to-market roles in the US; Toast US expansion and partnership scale-ups (GetYourGuide, LillyDirect, Tod's)

Operating leverage once the hiring wave laps: management remains 'confident in the inherent operating leverage of our business model over time' and says it chose not to chase 55% now; the 2022-23 cycle recovered from 43% to 55% by H2 2025

recent_developments.event: Q3 2026 Business Update (unaudited, revenue-only): net revenue €738.1mn, +23% / +22% CC ('in line with our full-year guidance'; company-compiled consensus €730.3mn per Reuters); volume €451.1bn, +30% (consensus €435.6bn); terminals 878k, +25%. Digital €387.4mn +16% / +14% CC; Unified Commerce €250.5mn +29% / +27% CC (incl. Talon.One); Platforms €100.2mn +46% / +44% CC (46 customers >€1bn, 312k active business customers). Talon.One/Orb consolidated for the first time (~2 points of CC growth; organic ~20% vs 21% in H1). FTEs 5,596 (+177 underlying, +399 acquired). Objectives: 2026 net revenue growth 21-23% CC (maintained); 'we now expect EBITDA margin of 50% in 2026' (prior ~51.7%); 'To retain flexibility, we are discontinuing our medium-term EBITDA objective' (prior: above 55% by 2028); CapEx 7% of net revenue (maintained); 2027 objectives in February 2027
recent_developments.significance: Small top-line beat and an unchanged growth guide, but the profitability reset dominated: long-run margin assumptions anchored on 55%+ by 2028 lose their anchor, making this the most valuation-relevant change since the Feb 2026 guide cut. Critics read it as another open-ended investment cycle like 2022-23 (stock3: '2023 vibes'; AlphaValue: 'Broken promises come at a price'); management frames it as deliberate growth investment

recent_developments.event: Business-update call (co-CEO Ingo Uytdehaage, interim CFO Hwa Tsao; Investing.com transcripts garble the names as 'Umlauf'/'Chua', so wording may be imperfect). Interim CFO: 'These are growth acquisitions, and we are doubling down'; 'We are intentionally deciding in 2026 to pull forward some of that spend'; no 'structural change' in cost of growth; some 2026 charges 'we don't expect to recur in 2027'; did not commit that 50% is a floor; people are the largest cost driver, equity pay 'a material contributor', 'I don't have a hard number for 2027' on SBC; Talon.One+Orb added ~2 points in Q3 with a similar Q4 contribution, shown only qualitatively; H2 'will shape up similar to the first half'; the Nov 2025 ~20% growth view was 'more kind of a guardrail as opposed to guidance'. Co-CEO: 55% would have been 'relatively easy' but 'at a risk of longer-term growth'; ~10% of volume is with a few hyperscale/cloud companies. S&P raised the outlook to positive (A- affirmed)
recent_developments.significance: Best primary evidence that the cut is a deliberate, uncapped choice; still missing are a floor, a 2027 margin or SBC number, and return milestones. Derived: a 22% CC full year needs Q4 of ~23-24% CC; repeating Q3's 22% gives ~21.5%

recent_developments.event: Market reaction: shares closed at €818.00 on 28 Oct vs €944.00 on 27 Oct (-13.4% on ~5.5x average October volume; Yahoo closes; early reports said -11% to -12%), then €815.90 (29 Oct) and €826.90 (30 Oct): -12.4% over three sessions, -39.9% YTD (€1,375.00 at end-2025), ~€26bn market cap, 52-week range €772.4-1,530.0. The post-H1 rally had already reversed (€1,090.40 on 28 Aug to €876.60 on 30 Sep, incl. -4.7% on 23 Sep after the CFO news; other September drivers not researched). Brokers: no downgrades found among those checked. Cuts: J.P. Morgan (Buy, €1,350 to €1,160, 29 Oct; removal of the target 'will disappoint the market'), Degroof Petercam (Buy, €1,300 to €1,150, off favourites list; 'clearly a nasty surprise'; consensus EPS -5-10%), AlphaValue (target -15.2%, 30 Oct). Citi kept Buy (€1,800; ~5% off consensus earnings); Jefferies ('net positive given the commitment to topline growth'), UBS, DZ Bank and Barclays kept Buy; Goldman Sachs had trimmed to €1,750 (Buy) around 7 Oct. MarketScreener 30 Oct: 34 analysts, Buy, average target €1,280.57 (range €863-1,800); Bloomberg's pre-cut average was just under €1,400. No post-drop insider purchases or activist filings found. Sources: Yahoo closes, Reuters, dpa-AFX, MarketScreener, trading-treff
recent_developments.significance: The de-rating is in the margin path, not the growth path: EPS estimates fall ~5-10% while ratings hold, so the debate becomes how long the investment phase lasts. Post-print views from Morgan Stanley (Overweight, €1,850 in Aug), Berenberg (Hold, €1,600) and BNP Paribas Exane (Neutral) were not found

recent_developments.event: Other Q3 release items: joined the ECB digital euro pilot as an acquiring PSP (ECB list of 36 PSPs published 14 Jul; pilot from H2 2027); partnered with Sierra and Meta on the 'Personal Agent Protocol', an emerging open standard for AI agents dealing with businesses; upgraded Authenticate ('double-digit conversion gains', company claim); scaled partnerships with GetYourGuide, LillyDirect, Tod's and Toast; early Talon.One/Orb cross-sell wins (Route, Wasabi Technologies)
recent_developments.significance: Strategically relevant (agentic commerce, new European rail) but not financially material near term; supports the 'full commerce lifecycle' case used to justify the spending step-up

recent_developments.event: EGM: shareholders approved Chris Vogelzang (Lloyds Banking Group director) to the Supervisory Board; Chair Piero Overmars retires 1 Nov 2026 and Herna Verhagen (ex-PostNL CEO) succeeds him; the EGM also discussed 'a governance update to Adyen's executive leadership model, which will take effect January 31, 2027' (no details found)
recent_developments.significance: Orderly board refresh, but an unexplained leadership-model change effective the day before the new CFO starts leaves the co-CEO structure an open question

recent_developments.event: Adyen nominated Niclas Neglen (Klarna CFO; earlier CFO and COO EMEA at HSBC Private Bank; 13 years at General Electric) as CFO and Management Board member, effective 1 Feb 2027 subject to an EGM vote and De Nederlandsche Bank approval; interim CFO Hwa Tsao covers until then and returns as SVP Group Finance. The release stated no change to financial objectives; the Q3 release repeated the nomination
recent_developments.significance: Ends the CFO search (shares -4.7% the next session), but the new CFO inherits a margin framework dropped five weeks later; the Feb 2027 results and 2027 objectives arrive around the handover

items.target: 21-23% YoY on a constant currency basis, including Talon.One and Orb (consolidated from 1 July 2026)
items.vs_prior: maintained (raised from 20-22% CC on 13 Aug 2026; the Q3 release calls Q3's +22% CC 'in line with our full-year guidance')
items.notes: Q3 CC +22% = ~20% organic + ~2 points from Talon.One/Orb (CFO: similar contribution in Q4); H1 was +21% CC, Q1 +20%. Reported growth for the first nine months (H1 plus Q3, which do not overlap) is +20.6%. The 22% midpoint needs Q4 of ~23-24% CC (derived); a Q4 repeat of Q3's 22% gives ~21.5%, in the lower half. CFO: H2 'will shape up similar to the first half', business is 'pretty lumpy', confident in the guide. MarketScreener consensus FY2026 net sales ~€2.87bn

items.target: 50% ('we now expect EBITDA margin of 50% in 2026')
items.vs_prior: CUT from ~51.7% (13 Aug guide: underlying margin in line with FY2025's 52.7% and ~1pp lower including acquisitions; Reuters described the prior level as about 52%). New 50% is ~1.7pp below that and 2.7pp below FY2025. The medium-term 'above 55% by 2028' objective is also DISCONTINUED (next item)
items.notes: Reason given: 'strong merchant interest' in the joint offer 'gives us the confidence to accelerate investments in our team, platform, and products'. H1 2026 was 49.2% (reported 49%; 50% excl. €6mn one-time deal costs), so FY 50% implies H2 of roughly 50-51% vs 55.0% in H2 2025. At ~€2.87bn net revenue, FY EBITDA of ~€1.43bn is ~€45-50mn below the old guide and H2 cash opex grows ~35% YoY (derived). Margin is stated after SBC (SBC sits in wages and salaries). CFO would not commit that 50% is a floor and said some 2026 charges will not recur in 2027

items.target: Discontinued ('To retain flexibility, we are discontinuing our medium-term EBITDA objective')
items.vs_prior: WITHDRAWN. The 'above 55% by 2028' objective (set at the Nov 2025 Investor Day) was reaffirmed in the Q1 update (May) and the H1 letter (13 Aug 2026)
items.notes: 'We remain confident in the inherent operating leverage of our business model over time.' On the call the co-CEO said the 2028 framework predated the acquisitions and that reaching 55% would be 'relatively easy' but 'at a risk of longer-term growth'; Adyen will instead give annual net revenue guidance plus qualitative colour on profitability and CapEx. The single most valuation-relevant change in this update

items.notes: H1 2026 CapEx was €64.1mn (~5%), so the full-year target implies ~€135-140mn or ~9% of H2 net revenue (derived). Historical framework was up to 5%; 2027 CapEx colour is due in February

items.vs_prior: not restated in the Q3 release; softened on the call
items.notes: CFO: 'The 20% that we put out in November was more kind of a guardrail as opposed to guidance.' Management would not promise acceleration or deceleration from the investment step-up

guidance.management_commentary: The Q3 update frames the margin cut as a growth call: 'Strong merchant interest in Adyen's joint value proposition across payments, loyalty, billing, and financial products gives us the confidence to accelerate investments in our team, platform, and products to capture the large opportunity we see ahead.' On the call (Investing.com transcripts; speaker names garbled) the interim CFO called the step-up deliberate, saw no structural change in the cost of growth and declined to call 50% a floor; people are the largest cost component, with small integration costs and higher equity compensation. The co-CEO said organic investment is always the first approach and that bolt-ons fill capability gaps. Capital-allocation priorities are unchanged (organic growth, then acquisitions, then shareholder returns). The call was hosted by co-CEO Ingo Uytdehaage and interim CFO Hwa Tsao; permanent CFO Niclas Neglen is due on 1 Feb 2027.

bull_case: Growth held at scale while investing: Q3 net revenue +22% CC (~20% organic), volume +30% (vs consensus €436bn), terminals +25% and the 21-23% CC guide intact. Management chose to spend ahead of the opportunity and says reaching the old 55% target would have been 'relatively easy'

Platforms (+44% CC, ~14% of revenue; 46 customers >€1bn vs 31 a year ago) and Unified Commerce (+27% CC; 499 customers at scale) keep diluting the slower Digital pillar, whose +14% CC comes with +28% volume, i.e. share-of-wallet gains with the largest customers

Talon.One/Orb demand is 'substantially stronger and broader than anticipated': Orb is a wedge into AI-native software (Route and Wasabi moved payments after Orb joined), Talon.One adds recurring non-volume revenue (~2 points of growth), and successful cross-sell could lift long-run growth above the ~20% 'guardrail'

Operating leverage is deferred, not lost: the 2022-23 hiring cycle took margin from 58.6% to 43.3% and it recovered to 55% by H2 2025 with growth intact; FCF conversion was 86% in H1, there is no financial debt, ~€4.6bn of own cash and an S&P outlook now positive; a ~50% EBITDA margin remains very high for payments

The de-rating may already reflect the lower margin path: €826.90 is -39.9% YTD and -24% from the 28 Aug peak, or ~21.5x 2026E and ~17.9x 2027E earnings on pre-revision consensus (MarketScreener); 34 analysts still rate it Buy (average target €1,281, +55%), with optionality in agentic commerce (Adyen Agentic, Personal Agent Protocol) and the ECB digital euro pilot
bear_case: No margin anchor and an open-ended investment cycle: 2026 margin cut to 50% (H2 ~50-51% vs 55.0% in H2 2025), the 55%+ by 2028 target dropped 11 weeks after being reaffirmed, no floor, no 2027 number until February, and the 2022-23 precedent shows margins can take ~2.5 years to rebuild; guidance credibility has been dented repeatedly

Rising equity compensation and dilution: pay 'increasingly emphasizes equity-based incentives' and equity is 'a material contributor' to the margin cut; SBC already rose from 1.84% of net revenue (FY2025) to ~2.2% (H1 2026) with no buybacks to offset issuance and no 2027 figure

Take rate and yield: 16.4bps in Q3 vs 17.2bps a year ago (organic ~16.1bps; the uptick vs Q2 is acquired non-volume revenue, not recovery); Digital volume +28% vs revenue +14% CC; ~10% of volume sits with a few hyperscale/cloud customers; Q3 volume +30% laps a weak base (Q3 2025 +8%, +19% excluding one large-volume customer)

Organic growth slowed to ~20% CC in Q3 (H1: 21%) with reported growth flattered by acquisitions (+2 points) and FX (+1 point); Digital is still the laggard (+14% CC), retail is 'subdued', and the ~20% medium-term view is now only a 'guardrail', so the spending step-up has not yet shown up as faster organic growth

Execution and governance load: interim CFO until Neglen starts on 1 Feb 2027 (subject to EGM/DNB approval), Supervisory Board chair change on 1 Nov, an undisclosed executive-leadership-model update on 31 Jan 2027, integration of 399 acquired FTEs on a ~+20% YoY headcount build, and CapEx of 7% (~9% in H2) squeezing free cash flow
key_metrics_to_watch: February 2027 (H2 2026 results): 2027 net revenue guide and whether a 2027 EBITDA margin, CapEx path and any new medium-term margin frame are given (today none exists; FY2025 52.7%, FY2026 guide 50%)
H2 2026 margin landing: FY 50% implies H2 EBITDA margin of ~50-51% (H1 2026 49.2%; H2 2025 55.0%) and H2 cash opex growth of ~35%; check that 2026 'one-time' charges actually fall away in 2027
SBC as % of net revenue (FY2025 1.84%; H1 2026 ~2.2%), equity-settled expense and share count (31.567mn at 30 Jun 2026): the first hard evidence of how 'equity-based' pay scales
Underlying hiring pace vs the 550-650 target (426 year to date) and total 1,000-1,100 (825 year to date incl. acquired); FTE 5,596 and revenue per FTE

Talon.One/Orb: ~2 points of quarterly growth (Q4 similar) with no segment disclosure, so watch FY-level revenue, qualitative cross-sell markers, purchase price allocation/goodwill and organic vs reported growth (Q3 organic ~20% CC)
Take rate: 16.4bps in Q3 (organic ~16.1bps) vs 17.2bps a year ago; does the 16.1-16.4bps range hold, and what is the rate ex-acquisitions
Digital growth (+14% CC) and the Digital volume-vs-revenue gap; Unified Commerce organic growth ex-Talon.One; Platforms customers >€1bn (46) and active business customers (312k)
CapEx: 7% of net revenue in 2026 (~9% implied in H2) and the 'towards historical levels' (up to 5%) path for 2027; FCF conversion (86% in H1)
CFO and governance milestones: EGM and DNB approval for Niclas Neglen (start 1 Feb 2027), Supervisory Board chair handover on 1 Nov, the executive-leadership-model update effective 31 Jan 2027
Sell-side revisions: EPS cuts of ~5-10% flagged by Degroof/Citi and low-single-digit for 2026 by J.P. Morgan; Morgan Stanley, Berenberg and BNP Paribas Exane stances; consensus target €1,281
